title: Union demands federal prison leaders be held in contempt after agency ‘openly defies’ court order
summary: The U.S. Bureau of Prisons director reportedly said in a meeting shortly before an injunction required him to restore the agency’s union contracts, “I don’t take directives from the court. I take my orders from the president.”

title: Social Security ends flexible work schedules, teeing up clash with union
summary: The agency’s top HR official says these changes are necessary to “deliver the service the public expects.” A union argues SSA violated its labor contract making this decision on its own.

title: Using holiday lights to inform hurricane recovery? Award honors ‘seemingly odd’ federally funded research that brings about groundbreaking discoveries
summary: The Trump administration has sought to upend federal support for scientific research, including through budget cuts and granting political appointees more control over the grantmaking process.

title: What happens when the State Department loses its institutional memory?
summary: COMMENTARY | With dozens of ambassadorial posts still vacant, the staffing of U.S. embassies is raising questions about the role of career diplomats and the experience needed to carry out American policy overseas.

title: Bureau of Prisons is the latest agency ordered to reinstate union rights
summary: As of Tuesday, at least one correctional facility has refused to recognize its union local, in apparent contravention of a preliminary injunction issued last week.

title: GSA still has problems with location data for federal properties, watchdog finds
summary: The agency has agreed to five recommendations aimed at improving the accuracy and management of the information.

title: FBI removes Accenture contractor after missed security patch led to breach
summary: The bureau’s cyber chief blamed a contractor’s failure to apply an available fix for an intrusion that may have exposed sensitive employee information.

title: TSA took away its officers’ chairs. The union isn’t sitting quietly
summary: The Trump administration has taken several actions to weaken Transportation Security Administration employees’ collective bargaining rights.

title: Appeals court seemingly OKs VA’s contested union contract expiration
summary: A three-judge panel found that a judge’s ruling in August forcing the VA to maintain its CBAs with AFGE improperly delved into questions of compliance with particular contract provisions.

title: Cut first, measure later: Watchdogs find problems across foreign affairs agency reorganizations
summary: Among the findings, the inspector general for the State Department reported that the government is spending $3.2 million biweekly on administrative leave for employees who received reduction in force notices last year.

title: US spy chief tapped as White House AI czar
summary: A new task force led by Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, will have 120 days to analyze and report on AI’s risks and opportunities, amid growing global calls for AI safety measures.

title: Transportation works to ease fears about its new AI air traffic control tool
summary: Rep. Don Beyer, D-Va., who has expressed skepticism about Transportation’s rollout of an AI-powered tool at D.C.-area airports, said he had “a good conversation” with FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford about the new capability that helped to alleviate some of his worries.

title: State Department appeals board, now with limited authority, gains new members
summary: The Trump administration recently limited the board’s authority to challenge employee removals and other adverse personnel actions, asserting that the secretary of state has final say on these decisions.

title: Housing finance agency chief moves to slash watchdog’s budget, leading Democrats to demand his resignation
summary: The Federal Housing Finance Agency inspector general said that budget cuts would force the office to reduce its staffing by up to 80% and effectively stop criminal investigations.

title: Federal employees’ health insurance premiums to rise by double digits for third straight year
summary: Some insurance carriers have undergone wide swings in cost, as at least one plan’s premiums will more than double next year.

title: GSA memo to set AI-specific acquisition rules
summary: The language includes changes some industry groups have requested through a public comment period and will go into effect Oct. 19.

title: Tax chief pushes 'AI-first IRS' to get more out of agency's workforce
summary: The IRS made more than 4,000 hires this year, but its headcount remains mostly unchanged after cutting more than a quarter of its workforce last year.

title: TSP funds were back in the negative in September
summary: The performance of portfolios in the federal government’s 401(k)-style retirement savings program largely mirrored market-wide declines.

title: Retiring in 2027? Picking the right date could pay off
summary: The date you leave federal service can affect when your annuity begins and how much you receive for unused annual leave.

title: Pentagon update on National Defense Strategy cites progress, omits key threats
summary: The report to Congress notes accomplishments but masks depleted arsenals, strategic distractions, and a quiet retreat from European defense.

title: EPA union sues management over contract termination
summary: AFGE accused EPA leadership of implementing President Trump’s executive order stripping many federal employees of their collective bargaining rights partly so it could discipline employees who signed an open letter criticizing Administrator Lee Zeldin more easily.

title: Trump’s new Education IG nominee continues dizzying run of leadership changes at the watchdog office
summary: Mark Priebe — the nominee, who recently served as acting inspector general at the Education Department — has defended the president’s mass firing of inspectors general and appears to have supported Trump on social media.

title: Judge extends temporary pause in USDA relocations as he considers indefinite freeze
summary: A federal judge in San Francisco said it was "significant" that Congress included a provision in a fiscal 2026 spending package that blocked the Agriculture Department from reorganizing without approval from the House and Senate appropriations committees.
